title: Getting started with scholid
text: scholid exposes small set user-facing functions operate consistently across identifier types: is_scholid(x, type) checks whether values match identifier type. normalize_scholid(x, type) returns canonical identifier strings. extract_scholid(text, type) extracts identifiers free text. classify_scholid(x) guesses identifier type per element. scholid_types() lists supported identifier types. generic helpers dispatch internally type-specific implementations is_doi(), normalize_orcid(), extract_isbn().

title: Getting started with scholid
text: is_scholid() checks whether value matches specific identifier type. vectorized preserves missing values.
code: x <- c(     "10.1000/182",     "not a doi",     NA ) scholid::is_scholid(     x    = x,     type = "doi"     ) ## [1]  TRUE FALSE    NA

title: Getting started with scholid
text: Normalization removes common wrappers enforces canonical representation. particularly useful identifiers stored URLs prefixed labels. ORCID iDs, normalization removes URL prefixes enforces hyphenated grouping. Normalization designed predictable: - NA input stays NA. - Invalid inputs typically become NA_character_.

title: Getting started with scholid
text: Extraction harvesting identifiers unstructured text. result list one element per input element. element character vector matches (possibly empty). list return type intentional: single text string can contain multiple identifiers.
code: txt <- c(   "See https://doi.org/10.1000/182 and doi:10.5555/12345678.",   "No identifier here.",   NA ) scholid::extract_scholid(     text = txt,     type = "doi"     ) ## [[1]] ## [1] "10.1000/182"       "10.5555/12345678." ##  ## [[2]] ## character(0) ##  ## [[3]] ## character(0)

title: Getting started with scholid
text: classify_scholid() returns best-guess identifier type per element mixed identifier columns. Classification based set available is_<type>() checks precedence order defined scholid_types().
code: x <- c(   "10.1000/182",   "0000-0002-1825-0097",   "PMC12345",   "2101.00001v2",   "not an id",   NA ) scholid::classify_scholid(x = x) ## [1] "doi"   "orcid" "pmcid" "arxiv" NA      NA

title: Getting started with scholid
text: Many identifiers appear wrapped (URLs, prefixes, trailing punctuation). Classification strict typically expects canonical strings. common pattern : Extract identifiers text. Normalize extracted values. Classify /validate.
code: txt <- "Read https://doi.org/10.1000/182 (and ORCID 0000-0002-1825-0097)." dois <- scholid::extract_scholid(txt, "doi")[[1]] orcids <- scholid::extract_scholid(txt, "orcid")[[1]]  dois_n <- scholid::normalize_scholid(dois, "doi") orcids_n <- scholid::normalize_scholid(orcids, "orcid")  scholid::classify_scholid(c(dois_n, orcids_n)) ## [1] "doi"   "orcid" scholid::is_scholid(dois_n, "doi") ## [1] TRUE scholid::is_scholid(orcids_n, "orcid") ## [1] TRUE

title: Getting started with scholid
text: scholid intentionally small conservative: uses base R runtime. Functions vectorized return stable types. Type-specific logic kept small is_*(), normalize_*(), extract_*() helpers. package designed low-level building block packages.

text: detailed usage patterns, including extraction text classification mixed identifier columns, see Get started vignette.
code: # list supported scholarly identifier types scholid::scholid_types() ## [1] "arxiv" "doi"   "isbn"  "issn"  "orcid" "pmcid" "pmid" # test whether values match a given identifier type scholid::is_scholid(   x    = "10.1000/182",   type = "doi" ) ## [1] TRUE # normalize identifiers to canonical form scholid::normalize_scholid(   x    = "https://doi.org/10.1000/182",   type = "doi" ) ## [1] "10.1000/182" # extract identifiers of a given type from free text scholid::extract_scholid(   text = "See https://doi.org/10.1000/182 for details.",   type = "doi" ) ## [[1]] ## [1] "10.1000/182" # classify the identifier type of each input value scholid::classify_scholid(   x = c(     "10.1000/182",     "0000-0002-1825-0097",     "not an id"   ) ) ## [1] "doi"   "orcid" NA
